content.text: All three sizes are rendered and verified. **Output:** `portrait.png` (1080×1350), `wide.png` (1200×1000), `sky.png` (300×600) — exact pixel sizes confirmed. **How it's built** - One template (`build.js`) emits `portrait/wide/sky.html`. A single root variable sets `html { font-size: 16px × scale }` and *every* metric is in `rem`, so scale is exactly 1× / 0.85× / 0.28× (verified: root rem 16 / 13.6 / 4.48px; CTA type 44 / 37.4 / 12.32px). No compounding, no per-size hand-tweaking of type. - Inter loaded via `@font-face` from the local variable TTF (`font-weight: 100 900`), confirmed active in all three renders. - Vertical fit: the page is a flex column; the photo band is the only grower (`flex:1`, capped at `40vh`). Portrait/wide give it their surplus; on sky it hits the cap and `justify-content: space-between` distributes the ~19px remainder as even breathing room instead of leaving a hole. **Defects found and fixed** 1. My first audit ran at the wrong viewport (`viewportSize` is ignored by `newPage`, defaults to 1280×720) — fixed to `viewport`, otherwise every geometry check was meaningless. 2. Wide's photo crop was landing on empty sky with the hill sliced off. Crop focus is now per-size (`object-position` 58% / 74% / 50%) so the horizon reads correctly at every aspect; sizing stays `object-fit: cover`, so it crops and never distorts. 3. Headline and "VOTE BY MAIL" had ink overflowing their line boxes (166px of glyph in a 164px block). Line-heights loosened to 1.18 / 1.15. The final audit reports **no issues** at all three sizes: bands full-bleed to the exact viewport width, candidate column centers evenly spaced (206.7/540/873.3 — 333.3 apart on portrait, likewise on the others), no element out of frame, no scroll overflow, no section overlap, and the photo `` exactly filling its band. One judgment call worth flagging: at 0.28× the sky's body copy lands at ~7px and the footer at ~5px, which is small but is the literal consequence of the specified scale — I kept the ratio faithful rather than silently bumping the small size's type.

A single root variable sets `html { font-size: 16px × scale }` and *every* metric is in `rem`, so scale is exactly 1× / 0.85× / 0.28× (verified: root rem 16 / 13.6 / 4.48px; CTA type 44 / 37.4 / 12.32px). Portrait/wide give it their surplus; on sky it hits the cap and `justify-content: space-between` distributes the ~19px remainder as even breathing room instead of leaving a hole. **Defects found and fixed** 1. My first audit ran at the wrong viewport (`viewportSize` is ignored by `newPage`, defaults to 1280×720) — fixed to `viewport`, otherwise every geometry check was meaningless. 2. Wide's photo crop was landing on empty sky with the hill sliced off. Crop focus is now per-size (`object-position` 58% / 74% / 50%) so the horizon reads correctly at every aspect; sizing stays `object-fit: cover`, so it crops and never distorts. 3. Headline and "VOTE BY MAIL" had ink overflowing their line boxes (166px of glyph in a 164px block). Line-heights loosened to 1.18 / 1.15. The final audit reports **no issues** at all three sizes: bands full-bleed to the exact viewport width, candidate column centers evenly spaced (206.7/540/873.3 — 333.3 apart on portrait, likewise on the others), no element out of frame, no scroll overflow, no section overlap, and the photo `` exactly filling its band. One judgment call worth flagging: at 0.28× the sky's body copy lands at ~7px and the footer at ~5px, which is small but is the literal consequence of the specified scale — I kept the ratio faithful rather than silently bumping the small size's type.
